turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning, Mrs. Cartwright. This is your routine blood pressure and cholesterol review, yes?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, Doctor. Yes, that is correct. My husband Robert asked to sit in, if that is agreeable.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Of course it is. Mr. Cartwright, take the chair by the wall. I tend to think out loud, so interrupt me if I lose the thread.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you. I'll only chime in when I'm sure of the fact.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Helen, any chest pain or chest pressure when you walk, since I last saw you?

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): If I may, before I answer that, I feel I should tell you that I stopped the cholesterol tablet. I read an article online about memory loss and muscle damage, and it alarmed me terribly.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll talk about that article, and I am not going to scold you. I do still need the chest-pain answer, though. Has there been any?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. There has been no chest pain at all. I apologize for answering a different question.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Happens all the time. Any shortness of breath, or swelling around the ankles by evening?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No shortness of breath, and my ankles have not swollen.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She gets headaches most afternoons, and it's been about three weeks. She won't bring it up herself.

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, Robert, that is not accurate. I would not call it a headache. One evening I felt a mild pressure behind the eyes, it eased when I sat quietly, and it has not returned. I cannot say when it started, perhaps last week, perhaps before that.

[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): All right, so we have two versions, a three-week run of afternoon headaches versus a single evening that resolved, somewhere between a few days and three weeks, and no firm date. With that pressure, any nausea, blurred vision, or weakness?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No nausea, no blurring, and no weakness. Otherwise I felt quite myself.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Now the medicines you actually take. Lisinopril for the blood pressure, ten milligrams by mouth, yes?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, ten milligrams by mouth. I still take it, but only every other day. The label says once daily. I am embarrassed to say so.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Some weeks she skips more than every other day. I watch the bottle.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not skip more than that, Robert. I am careful. I do occasionally lose track of which day I am on.

[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the prescription is daily, the habit is every other day, and extra missed doses are still a bit unclear. Noted, without a lecture. The cholesterol one was atorvastatin?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Atorvastatin, twenty milligrams by mouth at night. I stopped it five or six weeks ago, after three years of taking it. I cannot give the exact day.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I thought you were on forty milligrams, and that you stopped closer to two months ago.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, the bottle says twenty milligrams. I read it this morning. As for the date, well, I truly do not remember, so I will not pretend to.

[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then we keep twenty milligrams, and we leave the stop date approximate, five-ish weeks or longer, not a precise number. Were the muscles actually sore, or was it only the article?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the article, Doctor. I have had no muscle pain.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you added anything, fish oil, red yeast rice, someone else's pills?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing of my own. My husband takes metformin for his diabetes, five hundred milligrams twice a day. I have never taken his tablets.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please keep it that way. Those are not yours. Do you take anything else regularly?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): A baby aspirin, eighty-one milligrams, every morning. You had suggested it, and I do not miss that one.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Aspirin eighty-one each morning, still going. Any drug allergies?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I know of.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her mother used to say she developed a rash from penicillin as a child. We've been wary of it ever since.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I have no recollection of that, and a dentist gave me penicillin years ago with no reaction whatever. I do not consider myself allergic.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I won't record a penicillin allergy on that. If an old note ever turns up, we can reconsider. On the monitor, your pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-four, and the heart rate is seventy-two.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent, respiratory rate sixteen, temperature thirty-six point eight. All of that is reassuring.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear, the heartbeat is regular with no murmur, and there is no swelling at the ankles.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I am glad the examination is so ordinary.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me reason it out. Even on every-other-day lisinopril, one thirty-eight over eighty-four is acceptable for today, if not the number I'd love forever. The statin gap is the part I don't want to shrug off.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): I was concerned you would be displeased that I stopped it on the strength of a website. I even printed two pages, though I left them on the kitchen table beside Robert's crossword.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not displeased. The piece you read inflated the chance of muscle injury, and the memory claims haven't held up well in the studies I trust. What it didn't explain is that untreated cholesterol risk is silent, which is how it gets postponed.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Would you prefer that I resume the atorvastatin today?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. I want a fasting lipid panel and a metabolic panel, liver and kidney on the same blood draw, before we decide. We'll have those done this week.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I have already eaten, I'm afraid. Tea and toast before we left the house.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then tomorrow morning, fasting, is the better draw. I'll put both tests in as ordered, not as a maybe. The front desk can hand you the slip.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll drive her over. Mornings are easier with two of us.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, Robert. I will keep that appointment.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the lipids come back high, we might restart atorvastatin at ten milligrams instead of twenty. I am not prescribing it today.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I would wish to talk it through before any cholesterol tablet is started again.

[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's exactly why we'll sit down again. Separately, if muscle aches showed up after a restart, we might check a CK, the muscle enzyme. Only if that happens. Not on this visit.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): About the head pressure, I can't tidy it into one story. It might be simple tension, or it might tie to the blood pressure, and those are both still open.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. If it returns I will say so plainly.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd like to see you in a month, with the labs back, and revisit the statin decision then.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): One month is quite suitable.

[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please take the lisinopril every day again, ten milligrams by mouth once a day, keep the aspirin as it is, and leave the metformin alone. And if the head pressure comes back and stays, come in sooner rather than waiting the month.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall do all of that. Thank you for explaining your reasoning instead of simply directing me, and I will see you in a month.
